records.notes: Statement attributed by the book to the authors cited (Pithayanukul et al., 2010) about venoms of other species; one of four enzyme records sharing the same sentence.

records.role_detail: PLA2 inhibition, offered as a possible explanation for the antivenom effect (Hung et al., 2004)
records.mechanism_book_wording: correlation between antivenom activity of melanin and PLA2 inhibition
records.quote: Authors demonstrated correlation between antivenom activity of melanin and PLA2 inhibition as a possible explanation for the protective effect.
records.numbers_detail: 3 mg per mouse of melanin extracted from black tea, i.p., given immediately after venom injection (PDF page 590)
records.notes: Described as a correlation and a possible explanation, not as a demonstrated mechanism. Compound described as an unhydrolyzed complex of tea polyphenols.

records.mechanism_book_wording: Nonquantal ACh acting through M1-cholinergic receptors ... activates synthesis of NO
records.quote: Nonquantal ACh acting through M1-cholinergic receptors (Urazaev et al., 2000; Malomouzh et al., 2007), activates synthesis of NO
records.notes: Role Agonist is inferred from 'acting through ... receptors, activates'; the page does not use the word agonist. Background literature, not tested in this chapter.

records.mechanism_book_wording: Glutamate released from nerve endings probably activates NMDA-receptor mediated Ca2+ entry into the sarcoplasm
records.quote: Glutamate released from nerve endings probably activates NMDA-receptor mediated Ca2+ entry into the sarcoplasm
records.notes: Role Agonist inferred from 'activates NMDA-receptor'. NMDA receptor is an ionotropic receptor; recorded as receptor because the book calls it a receptor. Hedged by the book ('probably').

records.target: membrane acceptors (coupled to intracellular Ca2+ stores)
records.notes: Target class receptor is inferred: the book says 'acceptors' without naming a receptor protein, and calls it 'membrane acceptors coupled to intracellular Ca2+ stores' (PDF page 592). Role Agonist inferred from 'activating'. Listed as one of several proposed mechanisms for BthTX-I myotoxicity.

records.target: membrane acceptors (coupled to intracellular Ca2+ stores)
records.mechanism_book_wording: C. sinensis is able to inactivate the acceptors signalization
records.quote: By this mechanism, C. sinensis is able to inactivate the acceptors signalization.
records.notes: Target class receptor and role Antagonist are inferred. The chapter's conclusion (PDF page 594) says the extract acts by 'an unclear mechanism of action', and PDF page 593 says the actual molecular mechanism 'remains to be cleared'.

chapter_notes: Chapter content ends at PDF page 594 (conclusion), references on 594-598. Skipped 4 statements whose target is neither receptor nor enzyme (BthTX-I and Mn2+ at Ca2+ channel pore, Lys49 PLA2 homologues inactivating voltage-dependent sodium channels, ACh/NO keeping Cl- transport inactive). Also left out: the tea-polyphenol statement that they 'interact with hydrolytic enzymes' of Naja and Calloselasma venoms (PDF 590), because no inhibitor or activator role is stated, and BthTX-I itself (a Lys49 PLA2 homologue with lost enzymatic activity, per the book). The chapter's own experiments (Camellia sinensis extract, theaflavin, epigallocatechin gallate against venom or BthTX-I on mouse phrenic nerve-diaphragm) are reported as neutralization/protection with no named molecular target.
